channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: SparkLend borrowing against crypto collateral
item.description: When does it make sense to use SparkLend? It suits holders seeking DAI or USDS liquidity against ETH or BTC, provided rates and liquidation risk fit.

item.title: Private RPC Confirmation Time and Builder Inclusion
item.description: How long does a private RPC transaction take to confirm? Often one or a few 12-second slots; builder access and priority fee set the wait on Ethereum.

item.title: Lock-and-mint bridges: how tokens cross chains
item.description: How does lock and mint bridging work? The source tokens are locked, then validators relay a message so an equal representation can be minted on the destination chain.

item.title: Spender Address in a Token Approval: How ERC-20 Encodes It
item.description: What is the spender address in a token approval? It identifies who can transfer your tokens from your wallet, up to the allowance recorded by the token contract.

item.title: What Is an Automated Market Maker in Crypto, and How It Works?
item.description: What is an automated market maker in crypto? It is a smart contract that swaps tokens from pools, prices trades by formula, and lets you start with a wallet and gas.

item.title: Who Can Create a Pool When Factories Set the Rules
item.description: Who can create a token liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange? Anyone who meets its factory rules can; funding and token risk determine whether it is useful.

item.title: US court orders cover $1.2 billion in stolen Binance crypto
item.description: The Justice Department says court orders cover more than $1.2 billion of Binance funds, part of $2.7 billion frozen as tracing and forfeiture work continues.

item.title: Consolidating crypto across chains by separate transfers
item.description: How to consolidate crypto from multiple chains into one: choose a destination chain, bridge each spendable balance, and confirm every arrival before sweeping leftovers.

item.title: US targets $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance
item.description: The Justice Department says it has court authority to seize or restrain over $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance on Oct. 29, as tracing continues.

item.title: DAO votes: delegate first, then make your tokens count
item.description: DAO voting weights your token balance at a snapshot; learn when to delegate, how quorum and majority decide a proposal, and how the approved change is carried out.

item.title: Restaking Security for an AVS: The Stake Path
item.description: Restaking secures an AVS by putting delegated ETH or liquid staking tokens at risk under service rules, giving operators an economic reason to do the work correctly.

item.title: US secures seizure order for $1.2B in Binance hack
item.description: The Justice Department says a court order covers more than $1.2 billion of assets stolen in Binance’s $6.3 billion hack; tracing and recovery continue.

item.title: US wins authority over $1.2bn in Binance theft
item.description: The Justice Department won court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of Binance hack proceeds, part of $2.7 billion frozen so far.

item.title: What does a bridge aggregator do? It ranks cross-chain routes
item.description: seo_title: What is a bridge aggregator in crypto? Compare routes

item.title: How do wrapped tokens stay backed: Trace reserves and redemption
item.description: How do wrapped tokens stay backed by original assets? Controlled issuance, verifiable reserves and redemption rules link each wrapped claim to assets held in custody.

item.title: What Does Cryptoeconomic Security Mean for Restaked ETH?
item.description: Cryptoeconomic security in restaking means your ETH is the penalty: cheating should cost operators more than they gain, while AVS rules shape your risk.

item.description: US authorities have court approval to seize or restrain $1.2bn of crypto stolen from Binance, part of $2.7bn frozen as recovery efforts continue.

item.title: US court authorizes seizure of $1.2bn in Binance theft
item.description: The Justice Department says a court authorized seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion in crypto from Binance’s October theft; recovery efforts continue.

item.title: US gets court authority over $1.2bn in Binance theft funds
item.description: The Justice Department has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of Binance theft funds, while tracing and recovery efforts continue.
